observation.visible_scene: An underwater view looking upward toward the water surface, with bright sunlight breaking through the rippling surface and casting distinct god rays (light beams) down into deep blue water. Air bubbles of various sizes and fine suspended particles (marine snow) are scattered throughout the frame, with a denser cluster of bubbles along the left edge in the early frames. A small greenish lens-flare artifact flickers near the bottom center.
visible_changes: The bright sun patch and the fan of light rays slowly shift position across the top of the frame, moving from center-left toward the upper-right as the clip progresses, indicating a gradual camera pan/tilt or rotation relative to the surface.
The cluster of bubbles along the left edge in the first frames drifts upward/out of view and the left side becomes progressively emptier by the later frames.

A pair of bubbles on the right side moves steadily downward and to the right across the sequence (from roughly mid-frame-right toward the lower-right corner), consistent with camera motion re-framing them rather than the bubbles themselves sinking.
The surface ripple pattern and the angle/visibility of individual light shafts shimmer and change continuously frame to frame.
The green lens-flare artifact at the bottom center appears, fades, and reappears at slightly different positions.
Suspended particles drift slowly within the water column, changing relative positions frame to frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera is handheld, on a rig, or attached to a moving diver/subject is not shown.
The source or cause of the bubbles (e.g., a diver exhaling) is not visible within this segment.
What happens before the first frame and after the last frame is unknown; both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: It is ambiguous whether the apparent downward-right motion of the right-side bubbles and the leftward drift of the sun patch are due to camera movement, water motion, or the bubbles' own buoyant rise; the background surface provides limited parallax to disambiguate.
The exact depth and water clarity are inferred from appearance only.
